description_en: Teku Sataḥ, situated between Kũvera Sataḥ (KAT2618) and Kālo Pula (KAT2682), was damaged during the 2015 CE earthquakes. Following this, the resident Buḍhāthokī and Thāpā families dismantled the structure and built makeshift rooms for residential use, preserving and reusing one of its original wooden windows.An inventory from 1982 CE (VS 2039) includes a photograph of the original building, showing a five-columnphalcā(arcade) on the ground floor. This space had likely already been enclosed for residential use by around 1973 CE (VS 2030). The upper floor featured three wooden windows, and the roof was covered with traditionaljhiṃgiṭītiles. The same inventory refers to an inscription stating that thesataḥwas constructed around 1915–16 CE (VS 1972) by akājī(a high-ranking official) from Chāgaḍola, Kathmandu, although the name of the builder is not mentioned. The current residents are unaware of the whereabouts of this inscription. As of February 2025, it is no longer visible at the site, suggesting it may have been lost or relocated.Nearby, Dirghalakṣmī, the wife of Vīrabhadra Kũvara and sister-in-law of Balabhadra, is said to have built anothersataḥand a Śivālaya (Śiva shrine). This connection supports the hypothesis that the Teku Sataḥ was also built by akājīfrom the same Kũvara lineage.The Teku Sataḥ underwent a renovation in 1971–72 CE (VS 2028) (Inventory VS 2039, p. 165). In front of thesataḥlies abrahmanāla—a sacred site for bathing or performing oblations for the deceased before cremation. This indicates that the building likely served funerary functions: providing shelter for the terminally ill, hostingśrāddharites, and facilitating cremation rituals.There are no temples in the immediate vicinity, suggesting that the structure was not intended as a religious shrine or temple.According to oral accounts from the Buḍhāthokī (male, age 56) and Thāpā (male, age 59) families, a Kũvara descendant—who claims relation to the original builder—frequently visits the site.
description_ne: घाटमा दाहा संस्कार गर्दा, परिवार सदस्य मरनासन्न अवस्थामा पुग्दा घाटमा वासको व्यवस्था एवं श्राद्धका खातिर प्रयोगमा लिन राणाकालमा कुँवर खलकले यो सतः थपेको देखिन्छ ।यो सतः कुँवर सतः (KAT2618) र कालो पुल (KAT2682) को बीचमा अवस्थित छ । विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पमा क्षति भए पश्चात् यहाँ बस्दै आएका बुढाथोकी र थापा परिवारले सतः भत्काई जेनतेन कोठा निकाली आवासस्थलका रूपमा प्रयोग गर्दै आएको छ । विगत सतःमा भएका काँठको झ्याल बचाई पुनः प्रयोगमा ल्याइएको छ । काठमाडौं उपत्यका नगर विकास योजनाद्वारा विसं २०३९ (सन् १९८२) मा प्रकाशित एक इन्भेनटोरीमा सतःको पूर्वरूप देखिने फोटो प्रकाशित छ (Inventory VS 2039, p. 165) । उक्त फोटोलाई नियाल्दा सतःको भूमि तलामा पाँच कवलको फल्चा देख्न सकिन्छ । फल्चाका कवललाई विसं २०३० को दशकमै छोपी आवासीय प्रयोजन हुन थालिसकेको देखिन्छ । सतःको माथिल्लो तलामा तीनवटा काँठका झ्याल थिए । छानो परम्परागत झिँगटीले छाइएको थियो । विसं २०३९ सालमा प्रकाशित उक्त इन्भेन्टोरीमा यहाँ शिलापत्र भएको र यसका निर्माता काठमाडौंको छागडोल बस्ने कुनै काजि पदका व्यक्ति भएको उल्लेख छ । विसं १९७२ (सन् १९१५-१६) मा निर्माण भएको भनी मिति पनि तोकिएको छ तर काजि पदका निर्माताको नाम खुलाइएको छैन । यहाँ बस्दै आएका परिवार आफूलाई शिलापत्रबारे जानकारी नभएको बताउछन् । यस सतः नजिकै वीरभद्र कुँवर (बलभद्रका दाजु) की माहिली पत्नी दीर्घलक्ष्मीले बनाएको सतः र शिवालय अवस्थित छ । दीर्घलक्ष्मी कुँवरले कृति बनाएकै ठाउँमा सोही खलकका कुनै काजिबाट यो सतः थपिएको हुन सक्दछ । शिलापत्र हाराएकाले विस्तृत जानकारी खुल्न सकेको छैन । सतःको जीर्णोद्धार विसं २०२८ (सन् १९७१-७२) सालमा गरिएको थियो (Inventory VS 2039, p. 165) ।यस सतः कुनै देवस्थल वा मन्दिरलाई लक्षित गरी बनेको देखिदैन । यसको अगाडि-पछाडि कुनै मन्दिर छैन । तर, सतःको ठिक अगाडि ब्रह्मनाल बाँकी छ । यसर्थ घाटमा दाहा संस्कार गर्दा, जीवनको अन्तिम अव्स्थामा घाटमा वासको व्यवस्था एवं श्राद्धका खातिर प्रयोगमा लिन कुँवर खलकले यो सतः थपेको देखिन्छ । यहाँ रहँदै आएका बुढाथोकी र थापा परिवारका अनुसार निर्माताका दरसन्तान भनी बेलाबखत एक कुँवर खलक बेलाबखत आउने गरेका छन् (one of the family members, Budhathokī, male, age 56, one of the family members, Thāpā, male, age 59) ।
monument_assessment: Heavily damaged (collapsed, demolished, major cracks and structural damages), Rebuilt

historical_events.event_description: An inventory published in 1982 CE (VS 2039) refers to an inscription stating that akājīfrom Chāgaḍola, Kathmandu, built thesataḥaround 1915–16 CE (VS 1972), although the individual's name is not recorded. The current residents are unaware of the existence or content of this inscription. In the vicinity, Dirghalakṣmī—wife of Vīrabhadra Kũvara and sister-in-law of Balabhadra—constructed anothersataḥalong with a Śivālaya, suggesting that the Teku Sataḥ may also have been built by akājīfrom the same Kũvara lineage. However, due to the loss of the inscription, further details remain unavailable.
Thesataḥunderwent renovation in 1971-72 CE (VS 2028) (Inventory VS 2039, p. 165).

The historicsataḥwas badly damaged in the 2015 earthquake, consequently demolished, and rebuilt as a simple brick and mortar shack, covered with a corrugated metal roof.Only one historic carved window was reused in the new building. All other historic materials, such as carved windows, doors, columns etc., were lost.
